title: Priority-weighted quota slicing and overage escrow for multi-plan customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a priority-weighted quota slicing mechanism and an 'overage escrow' billing flow so customers with multiple plans or priorities can (1) allocate a single aggregate entitlement across controllers/routes with weights, (2) incur overage charges in a staged escrow model to avoid immediate invoice shock, and (3) allow automated reconciliation and rollback for disputed overage within a short window.
background: Large enterprise customers frequently run mixed workloads across multiple product lines and want a single entitlement pool while preserving priority for critical routes (e.g., customer-facing chat vs. batch analytics). Current per-plan hard quotas force costly plan juggling or manual reconciliation. Existing soft-overage features provide immediate overage charges which leads to invoice disputes and churn. We need a solution that supports weighted allocation, prioritized throttling when capacity is constrained, and a delayed/escrowed overage charge that can be auto-reconciled with credits or rollbacks.
goals: 1) Allow a tenant to declare an aggregate compute/usage entitlement and attach named priority buckets with configurable weights. 2) At runtime, route requests against priority buckets and consume quota proportionally to weights, falling back to graceful degradation for low-priority buckets when headroom is low. 3) When aggregate consumption exceeds entitlement, place overage on an escrow ledger that appears in billing UI but is billed only after a 7-day dispute window. 4) Provide clear metrics in Console and per-route attribution for cost and token usage.
non_goals: 1) This work does not change base unit pricing or currency conversions. 2) We will not implement per-token dynamic pricing for this initiative. 3) The escrow model will not apply to monthly committed reserved capacity (Dedicated contracts) in the first phase.
requirements: API: POST /entitlements/aggregate to create aggregate entitlements with total_credits and priority_buckets (name, weight, default_route_list)
API: PATCH /entitlements/{id}/weights to adjust bucket weights in real time with validation against min/max percent constraints
Runtime: Router must accept 'priority-bucket' header and deduct usage from aggregate entitlement according to weight-proportional algorithm
Fallback: Low priority buckets should receive configurable degradation policies (throttle, queue, model-swap) when projected consumption in next 60s exceeds headroom
Billing: Overages recorded to escrow ledger with fields (amount_estimate, timestamp, routes_contributing, window_expires_at)
Console: New Entitlements page showing aggregate pool, per-bucket consumption, projected days-to-exhaust, escrowed overage amount and dispute controls
Alerts: Per-tenant alert rule when projected exhaustion within 24h with recommended actions (reduce weight, enable throttles, purchase top-up credits)
Data: Generate audit log entries for weight changes, overage ledger writes, and disputed-rollbacks for compliance
Docs: Public API docs and developer guide with examples for common scenarios (chat-first customer, analytics-first, hybrid)
Telemetry: Emit metric labels ent.pool_id, ent.bucket, ent.weight, ent.allocated_tokens, ent.consumed_tokens for SLOs and billing reconciliation
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant with aggregate entitlement of 1,000,000 token-credits and two buckets (critical weight=70, secondary weight=30), when concurrent traffic consumes tokens, the runtime deducts credits proportionally; critical bucket consumption will reflect ~70% of aggregate usage over a 10-minute rolling window

When projected consumption indicates exhaustion within 24 hours, the Console shows a warning and the tenant receives a notification; the suggested mitigation list includes weight adjustment, enabling bucket-level throttles, or purchasing top-up credits

If consumption exceeds aggregate entitlement, overage events are written to escrow ledger and visible in Console with a clear 'dispute by' timestamp set to 7 days from event; no invoice chargeable amount is generated until escrow settles

Escrow settlement flow: if no dispute is raised within the 7-day window, the escrowed amount is posted to the next invoice. If a dispute is raised and approved, the escrow ledger entry is auto-voided and credits are returned to aggregate entitlement

Runtime fallback behavior validated: low-priority bucket receives configured throttle response (429 with Retry-After) when headroom drops below configured threshold and high-priority routes continue serving with degraded latency within SLO

APIs validated with unit and integration tests: entitlement creation, weight adjustment, overage ledger writes, dispute creation, and settlement endpoints should return documented status codes and error messages
Console displays per-route attribution for at least 90% of escrowed overage events (routes_contributing populated) and per-bucket consumption graphs for last 30 days
Audit logs include immutable entries for weight changes and overage ledger events for compliance and are retained according to retention policy (90 days visible, archived afterward)
rollout_plan: 1) Alpha: internal-only rollout for 3 enterprise customers with dedicated account managers for 2 weeks. 2) Beta: opt-in for select customers in the billing sandbox with UI and API access for 6 weeks. 3) GA: enable for all tenants with Console UI and default 7-day escrow window; enable feature flag to disable escrow for dedicated contracts.
risks: 1) Complexity in attribution could lead to mis-billed customers; mitigate by conservative alpha and manual audit. 2) Escrow window may be abused for delayed payment; limit total escrow exposure per tenant and require enterprise contracts to pre-authorize billing. 3) Runtime overhead for weight calculations under high QPS; optimize with approximate window counters and sampling.
open_questions: 1) What is the maximum allowed number of priority buckets per entitlement? Recommend max 10. 2) Should escrowed amounts count against payment failure thresholds? Propose they do not trigger delinquency until settled. 3) Do we support retroactive weight rebalancing for historical attribution? Technical feasibility TBD.
notes: This ticket aims to reduce billing disputes and provide customers smoother operational controls when running mixed-priority workloads. Coordinate with Sales and Account Management to collect pilot candidates and draft customer-facing playbook.
